title: What is known about 1RB1LA_1RC0LD_1LB0RE_0LA0LC_0RD1RF_0RB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LA_1RC0LD_1LB0RE_0LA0LC_0RD1RF_0RB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open, not decoded. A multi-level counter on a background of 110: copies of a unit t^13 D are added one by one while a reservoir on the right is used up, then units of size 51, 241, 1191 appear in turn, each level built while the one before is consumed. This page shows the levels; no rule has been proved.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 70,849 cells have been visited and 35,479 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Units of growing size, to 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: Written with t = 110 and the defect D = 0 t^2 1 0 1 0, the tape is a sequence of units t^s D. In direct simulation the unit sizes come in levels s = 13, 51, 241, 1191 (ratios about 4, 4.7, 4.9): units of one level are added one at a time at the left end of the active region, about six t of a reservoir on the right being spent for each, and when the reservoir is empty the next level's units are built. No halt.

claims.title: The level-1 rule, with its step count
claims.text: With t = 110, the unit U = t^13 0 t^2 1 0 1 0 and the left end P = 1 0 t 1 0 1 0: the tape P U^n t^(r+6) with the head in E on the blank cell at its right becomes P U^(n+1) t^r with the head again in E at the right, after exactly 972n + 48r + 1014 steps. Four sweeps add one unit and use six t; the tape grows by 14 cells on the left and 18 on the right. Checked by direct simulation for all n ≤ 8, r ≤ 12 (117 cases); from blank tape it first applies at step 6,335 with n = 2, r = 5. Not proved in Lean: the symbolic prover does not find the rule, because a sweep does not cross a unit as one shift.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.25×10<sup>14</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 1.25×1014 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.41×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 546 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: The rule by which a level is built from the one before it, and what happens at the moment a reservoir runs out (where a halt, F reading 1, could occur), have not been written down; the question is not reduced.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LC_1LA0RE_0LD0LB_1RA1LD_0RC1RF_0RA--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LC_1LA0RD_0LD1LF_0RE0RA_1LB1RE_0LB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is made of units of a repeated word, and the machine counts them in levels, each level's units several times longer than the last. This page shows the levels; the rule between them has not been found.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 70,849 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Unit sizes of the first four levels.
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.41×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: Counters made of counters
html: Read the tape in the word t = 110. Almost all of it is t repeated, broken by a defect D = 0 t^2 1 0 1 0, so the tape is a list of units t^s D and a block of plain t at the right end, the reservoir.
Every few sweeps one more unit t^13 D appears at the left, and the reservoir shrinks: by 1, 1, 3 and 1 copies of t in four sweeps, six per unit. So level 1 counts the reservoir down in steps of six.

When the reservoir is empty the head eats into the next unit on its right and the process starts again with longer units, 51, then 241, then 1191 copies of t. By step 109 a second background has appeared to the right of the head, u = 100, in blocks u^1194 1 0 that are turned into units t^1191 D one at a time, the leftmost levels standing still:

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.57).
After 109 steps the tape spans 70,849 cells (2,226 left of the start, 54,876 right), with a density of 1s of 0.501.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: The step between levels
html: Each level is a simple countdown, of the kind symtm proves easily. What is missing is the transition: how the sizes 13, 51, 241, 1191 and the counts of each level are produced, and whether the transition can ever meet the halting cell. That is the work left for this machine.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A multi-level counter on a 110 background: units t^13 D added while a reservoir drains, then levels of size 51, 241, 1191. Not decoded.
